findings.text: `RuleStats.outcomes` repeats the allowed outcomes as a literal inside the counting mechanism. Fix: construct the counters from the documented `OUTCOMES` definition.
The docstrings for `log_path`, `append`, and `read` describe their results or operations but omit their purpose. Fix: explain the test override and how persistence supports review history.
The unknown-finding error gives no corrective action. Fix: tell the user to copy a finding ID printed by `just review` and select the corresponding log.

Logging failed and malformed reviews is new behavior without a test that verifies those records are written. Fix: add tests that exercise reviewer failure and malformed output and assert the resulting failure records.

The v4 replay test retains an inline 60-second limit, so valid replays between 60 and 120 seconds still fail despite the increased timeout. Fix: compare elapsed time against `replay_tiers.PHASE_LIMIT_SECONDS` and assert that the reported limit matches it.

When `CONFORMANCE_UPSTREAM` is set to an empty string, `Path('')` becomes `.`, so the message says "has no test directory: ." and does not tell the user that the variable is empty. If the current directory happens to contain a `test` directory, the empty value is accepted with no error. Fix: check for an empty value before the path check and fail with a message that says the variable is set but empty and must point to the pinned SQLite source archive.

The bundle checker's replay chain (`schemaEnvironment` and `checkBundle`, lines 115 and 124-129) now goes through `Environment.toKernelEnv.replay` and `Environment.ofKernelEnv`, which changes how the kernel gate builds the trusted and checked environments; owner review required. Fix: have the owner confirm that the kernel replay API in Lean 4.34.1 gives the same checks as the removed `Environment.replay`, including the axiom audit and target comparison on the result of `ofKernelEnv`.

The proof checker's three replay steps (lines 20, 22 and 25) now use `toKernelEnv.replay` and `Environment.ofKernelEnv` in the kernel gate; owner review required. Fix: have the owner confirm that the replayed environment passed to `checkTarget` still holds all declarations replayed by the kernel.

The export path now uses lean4export v4.34.0 (`076e8e57…`). Its upstream `dumpConstant` also skips `partial` declarations unless unsafe export is on (see the patch context at `build-support/lean4export-skip-trusted.patch:23`); owner review required. Fix: have the owner review the new exporter pin and the changed skip condition before the bundle path is accepted.

The changed message "The verifier requires the pinned Lean 4.34.1 runtime" does not name the Lean version that was found, or its sysroot, and does not say what the user can do next. Fix: include the detected version and sysroot, and tell the user to set `MIGRATION_CHECK_LEAN_SYSROOT` to a Lean 4.34.1 installation or to reinstall the verifier.

The pinned Lean version is a string literal inside the `locate` check, and the error message on the next line repeats it, so this commit had to edit the pin in two places. Fix: define a named constant such as `PINNED_LEAN_VERSION` with a docstring, and use it in both the check and the message.

The message tells every user to set `MIGRATION_CHECK_LEAN_SYSROOT`, but the installed entrypoint overwrites that variable (`build-support/runtime.nix:34`), so for an installed verifier this advice does nothing; `docs/install.md:33-35` already separates the two cases. Fix: tell installed users to reinstall the verifier, and limit the `MIGRATION_CHECK_LEAN_SYSROOT` advice to a development checkout, as `docs/install.md` does.

The new sentence "Reinstall the verifier." now sits between "Lean 4.34.1" and "set MIGRATION_CHECK_LEAN_SYSROOT to that installation", so "that installation" can be read as the reinstalled verifier, not a Lean 4.34.1 installation. Fix: write "set MIGRATION_CHECK_LEAN_SYSROOT to a Lean {PINNED_LEAN_VERSION} installation", which matches `docs/install.md:35`.

This commit changes the export path: `export_bundle` now omits declarations based on the closure of the bundle header's trusted imports plus `PROTECTED_BASE_MODULE`, through a merged search path, instead of using `--skip-trusted`; owner review required. Fix: have the owner review and approve the new omission set and the merged import view before release.

The new `migration-proof-exporter` replaces the patched lean4export executable and decides which declarations are left out of the bundle by marking the trusted import closure as visited; owner review required. Fix: have the owner review the omission logic in `importClosure`, `baseConstants` and `exportProof`, and record the approval in `plans/20261006-proof-exporter-owner-review.md`.

The docstring of `importClosure` says only what the function computes, not why the exporter needs the closure. Fix: say that the closure lists the modules the checker imports, so that exactly their declarations can be left out of the export.

findings.text: The CLI error message hard-codes the "10 GiB" capacity policy, which `tools/check_resources.py` already defines as `MIN_FREE_BYTES`, so the two can drift apart. Fix: build the message from `MIN_FREE_BYTES`, or let `check_resources` report the threshold.

The default engine version `'3.51.0'` and the `'sqlite3-' + version` library-name rule are literals inside `bindings`, copied from the recorder's version selection. Fix: use one named definition with a docstring, shared with `native_record.py`, to choose the engine version and library name for a record.

The message "Native replay receipt requires explicit storage and a path outside capture and corpus" does not tell the user what to do next. Fix: name the given receipt path and tell the user to supply `--temporary-root` and a receipt path outside the capture and output directories.

No test covers the changed freezer CLI: the required `--temporary-root`, the `check_resources` refusal, and the receipt name that is derived from `--output`. The tests call only `freeze()` directly. Fix: add a subprocess test with a timeout that checks the refusal without `--temporary-root` or with bad storage, and checks the location of the `<output>-native-replay.json` receipt.
`fresh = []` has no type hint. Fix: annotate it as `fresh: list[dict[str, Json]] = []`.

The `valid` case runs the real freezer CLI in a subprocess, where `check_resources` measures real free disk space, so the test fails on a host with less than 10 GiB free on the workspace, temporary or Nix-store filesystem (the other tests patch `shutil.disk_usage` for this reason). Fix: run the CLI through `main()` in-process with `shutil.disk_usage` patched, or skip the `valid` case with a clear reason when free space is below `MIN_FREE_BYTES`.

The new message says the receipt "requires explicit storage outside {directory} and {output}", which tells the user that the storage directory must be outside those directories, but the check requires the receipt path to be outside them and requires `--temporary-root` separately. Fix: give two clear requirements, for example "Native replay receipt {storage_report} must be outside {directory} and {output}, and --temporary-root must be given; select a receipt path outside both directories".

reason: The declared development environment requires at least MIN_FREE_BYTES (10 GiB) before expensive work. This real CLI check deliberately exercises that resource guard; insufficient space is a prerequisite failure that AGENTS requires us to report, rather than hide through a skip or mocked successful capacity. The small test does not materially consume the required budget.

findings.text: When `--temporary-root` is missing but the receipt is already outside both directories (the case the test at `tests/test_native_replay_storage.py:123` triggers), the message reports the receipt location as the problem and does not say that `--temporary-root` is missing. Fix: raise a separate message for each failed condition, one for a missing `--temporary-root` and one for a receipt path inside `{directory}` or `{output}`, and test both.

Fix: add `linux/full.json` to the commit (for example with `jj --config snapshot.max-new-file-size=2242637` or stored compressed as `full.json.gz`), and update the README, `sha256.json`, `validate.py` and `measure.py` to match.

`validate.py` reads `linux/full.json` and its hash is in `sha256.json:12`, so on a checkout of this commit the documented check `validate.py --source-root ...` stops with `FileNotFoundError`. Fix: commit the file it reads (or its compressed form), then run the validator again on a clean checkout.

The representative selection, the filesystem-type check and the receipt pass/fail logic in `measure.py` are new behavior, and no test covers them. Fix: move the selection into a pure function and add a short test that checks the selected cases and the tie-break against a small fixture list.

`SELECTION_POLICY` describes the selection rule only as text; the rule itself is written separately inside `main`, and no test links the two. Fix: put the rule in a named function whose docstring is the policy, and record that function's description in the receipt.

Fix: check each condition separately, give a message that names the field and the file, and say what to do (for example, select the original source or get the receipt again).

"Retained evidence bytes changed: NAME" says what failed but not what the user can do next. Fix: add the next step, for example "Restore the file from the commit that added it, or record new evidence in a new report directory".

"Three deterministic representative cases are required" does not say which input failed or what to do next. Fix: name the corpus path and how many authored cases and upstream source files it has, and tell the user to select a corpus with one authored case and two upstream source files.

"Fresh native observations differ from frozen evidence" does not name the case or the storage root, or say what to do next. Fix: include `record['name']` and `storage` in the message, and tell the user to compare the retained child output with the frozen record.

findings.text: The Darwin bundle prebuild copies the sandbox and fallback policy (`--option sandbox true`, `--option sandbox-fallback false`, the experimental features) as literals inside `run_checks`, and the `justfile` test recipes already state the same policy, so the two can drift apart. Fix: Define the hardened `nix-build` options once as a named constant with a docstring, or add a `just` recipe for the bundle target, and use it in `run_checks` and the test.

Each check in the validator is a bare `assert` with no message, so a failure shows only `AssertionError` and a line number: it does not say which payload or field failed, or what the user can do next. Fix: Raise errors with messages that name the file or field that failed and say how to find the cause, for example "compare raw-sha256.json with the retained gzip files".

The expected counts 16, 12 and 42 are literals inside `validate`, and only the docstring of `RAW_MANIFEST_SHA256` explains one of them. Fix: Define named constants with docstrings, for example `RETAINED_PAYLOAD_COUNT`, `ORIGINAL_PAYLOAD_COUNT` and `BUNDLE_CASE_COUNT`, and use them in `validate`.

`NIX_TEST_BUILD_OPTIONS` copies the sandbox policy that the `justfile` recipes still write as literals (lines 54, 58 and 86), and the new assertion in `tests/test_ci_checks.py` only compares the constant with another copy of the same literal, so the two definitions can still drift apart. Fix: Make one source of the policy and use it in both places (for example a `justfile` variable that `ci_checks.py` reads), or add a test that checks `NIX_TEST_BUILD_OPTIONS` against the options in the `justfile` test recipes.

This commit records v0.1.2 as published, but the release how-to still tells the reader to run `jj tag set v0.1.2` and `git push origin refs/tags/v0.1.2`, and its status text (lines 108-111) still names v0.1.1 as the latest stable release. The same section says never to reuse a released tag, so following the example now breaks that rule. Fix: change the example tag to a placeholder or the next unused version (for example `v0.1.3`), and add the v0.1.2 publication record next to the v0.1.1 record.

The new dependency check lacks a negative regression for package-style imports and skips `from conformance import replay_tiers`, allowing undeclared frontend dependencies in that module to pass. Fix: resolve imported submodules and add a regression that rejects an undeclared dependency reached through this import form.
`build-support/README.md` still describes seven targets and excludes only `model` from development checks. Fix: update it to describe all nine targets and the exclusion of both `model` and `frozen`.
The new `CONFORMANCE_SUITES` and `LOCAL_PACKAGES` policy lists have no docstrings. Fix: document why each list defines the dependency check’s scope.

The new `imported_modules`, `module_file`, `import_closure`, and `declared_frontend` docstrings describe their results without explaining their purpose. Fix: state each helper’s role in detecting undeclared Nix inputs.
The 600-, 300-, and 900-second limits are literals inside `main` rather than documented policy definitions. Fix: define named timeout constants with docstrings and use them in the command calls.
The new cache configuration retains a fallback to the replaced `nix-tests-v1` key scheme. Fix: remove the v1 restore prefix.

A failed Nix command raises before its captured stderr is printed, leaving users without the failure diagnostic or corrective action. Fix: report the captured diagnostic, failed command, and recovery guidance before exiting.

reason: One-time migration: without the v1 fallback the first run on each platform starts from an empty store, which may exceed the 30-minute job limit on macOS. Remove the line after both platforms have saved v2 caches.

findings.text: The failure message claims no store paths were removed even when `nix-store --gc` fails after partial deletion. Fix: distinguish failures before collection from collection failures, and report that collection may be incomplete.
The new collection-failure message gives no action the user can take next. Fix: tell the user to inspect the reported Nix error, correct its cause, and run the workflow again.

The existing collection-failure test passes without the new recovery guidance, so it does not protect this behavior change. Fix: extend the test to assert that the diagnostic tells users to correct the reported Nix error and run the workflow again.

The new `DeclaredType` docstring no longer says why the model keeps the type spelling apart from the affinity; the old text gave that reason, which is the rowid trap (a BIGINT primary key does not alias the rowid, but INTEGER does). Fix: say that the model keeps the spelling because it decides whether a primary-key column aliases the rowid.

The new `Column.plain` docstring says what the test checks but not why: `Execution.lean` uses it to admit only plain columns in CREATE TABLE and ADD COLUMN. Fix: say that the supported subset admits only plain columns in created and added columns, so the model does not need NOT NULL, defaults or alias spellings there.

The new `maximumColumns` docstring no longer gives the reason for 2000: the old text said that the value is SQLite's default ordinary-table column limit, and "the current model's fixed column bound" makes it look like an arbitrary model choice. Fix: say that 2000 is SQLite's default column limit (`SQLITE_MAX_COLUMN`) and that the profile fixes it at that value.

The new `statisticsColumns` docstring describes how the columns are built but no longer says why: they are the typeless column shapes that SQLite gives its engine-managed `sqlite_stat1` and `sqlite_stat4` tables. Fix: add one sentence that these are the exact typeless columns that SQLite creates for its statistics tables, which `supportedExistingTable` admits.

The new `normalizeIdentifier` docstring says what the function does but not why: the old text said that SQLite compares identifiers with ASCII-only case folding. Fix: say that the function copies SQLite's identifier comparison, which folds ASCII letters only, also in quoted identifiers.

The new `Schema` docstring removed the reason that the old text gave: schema order is kept for generated artifacts, and lookup depends on unique names. Fix: add back that the list keeps order for generated artifacts, and that `Schema.Valid` makes the names unique for lookup.

The new `Schema.emptyDatabase` docstring removed the reason for the definition (an empty, finite database to use in executable schema calculations), and "proof obligation" describes the application, not SQLite. Fix: say that the function gives an empty database with the given schema for executable schema calculations, and that the caller must show `Table.Valid` separately.

"Empty rows satisfy both checks" can mean rows with no cells, and that reading is wrong: with an empty key in `table.properties.keys`, `keyEqual` is vacuously true, so two such rows fail `uniqueRows`. Fix: write "A table with no rows satisfies both checks", or name the empty-key exception.

The tip "Omit such properties when neither is needed" comes with `{assert}`properties.uniqueKeys = []``, but that only says this example has no UNIQUE constraints and does not show the value to use when no properties are needed. Fix: give the value to use with a checked term, for example `{lean}`TableProperties.mk [] [] []`` or `{assert}`TableProperties.keys {} = []``, or remove the unrelated assert.

This commit changes the verification-target file: it changes the import, rewrites the `VerificationConditions` docstrings, and moves `of_run`/`congr_run`/`violates_required_schema` out of the file. Owner review required. Fix: get the owner's review of the changed verification-target file before release.

The `match` over `Statement` in `SchemaOnly` uses a catch-all `_ => False`, so a new constructor is silently excluded and causes no compile error. Fix: list `beginTransaction`, `commit`, `rollback`, `insert` and `update` as separate `False` cases.

`advance_schemaOnly` is a library lemma that other proofs use (`runSqlFrom_schemaOnly_append` and `runSqlFrom_extends` in `Preservation.lean`), but its docstring has no proof sketch. Fix: add one sentence that says the proof does a case split on the statement and uses the guard to exclude the transaction and literal-write branches.

The new module has no module docstring that gives its reason; the only module comment is the example block at the end. Fix: add a `/-! ... -/` docstring after the imports that says why the schema-only SQL lemmas are separate from `SqlExecution.lean`.
The new module has no module docstring that gives its reason. Fix: add a `/-! ... -/` docstring that says why the proof helpers for the verification target are separate from `Contract.lean`.

reason: Final owner review of the verification-target file and forthcoming protected schema baseline is explicitly required by the approved T05 task. Its target formulas are unchanged; this implementation and Claude review do not constitute owner approval.

findings.text: The docstring says the function "shadows" the transition, but it only returns source text from `def step` to the last namespace closure. It does not say that `step` must stay the last declaration in `Execution.lean`, which is a real trap: a declaration added after `step` would be copied into each mutant without any warning. Fix: say that the function extracts the text from `def step` to `end SqliteVerifier`, and warn that it requires `step` to be the last declaration in the namespace.

reason: Document the exact declaration/namespace span and the final-declaration requirement. The real error-seeking mode and four source regressions pass.

Fix: say that the function copies the text from `def step` up to the last `end SqliteVerifier` in `Execution.lean`, and warn that `step` must stay the last declaration in that namespace.

findings.text: The exempt step name is a policy literal inside the guard check. Fix: define a documented constant for the exempt step and use it in both assertions.
The `check_job_steps` docstring describes its output without explaining its purpose. Fix: state that it supplies step conditions to verify that macOS pull requests skip working steps.

The allowed non-project import roots `{"Init", "Std"}` are a literal inside the traversal in `visit`, and so are the project prefixes at line 38. Fix: define named constants with docstrings, for example `ALLOWED_EXTERNAL_IMPORT_ROOTS` and `PROJECT_MODULE_PREFIXES`, next to `APPLICATION_MODULES`, and use them in `visit`.

The commit adds copies of the model modules, the conformance laws and the structural codec, but the originals in `SqliteVerifier/`, `VerifierConformance/Laws.lean` and `StructuralCodec.lean` stay in use, so two parallel implementations of the model now exist and can drift apart. Fix: Move the modules and update their callers in one change, and delete the originals, so that only one copy of each model module exists.

The module docstring of a model file refers to an ADR number and to "the verifier" rather than to SQLite behavior. Fix: State what the laws assert about SQLite transaction and statement execution, without the ADR reference or the application.

The docstring of `body_rollback` says that the body "cannot change a transaction's original snapshot", but the formula says that running the body followed by ROLLBACK, from a state whose snapshot is `original`, succeeds with exactly `original`. Fix: Restate the assumption (each body statement succeeds and is not transaction control), the appended ROLLBACK, and the result `.success original`.

`body_rollback`, which `rollback` uses, and `literal_cases` (line 34), which `statement_atomicity` uses, are library theorems with no proof sketch. Fix: Add a 1-5 sentence sketch to each: induction over `SuccessfulBody`, and a case split over the statement and the table lookup.

The `GeneratedInputs` docstring in the model package refers to "application declarations" and "verification conditions". Fix: Describe the record only in terms of SQLite profiles, schemas and statements.

The message "unsupported generated-inputs version" does not give the version it received or the supported version, and it does not tell the user what to do next. Fix: Include the received version, say that only version 1 is supported, and tell the user to regenerate the inputs with a matching frontend.

findings.text: The commit updated `prepare_examples.py` but not this caller of `cli.verify`: it still catches only `Rejection`, so a parser, profile or admission refusal now raises the new `SqlError` and stops the trial with a traceback instead of recording its status. Fix: catch `(Rejection, SqlError)` here, the same way `migration_check/cli.py:106` does.

The module docstring, which is the diagnostic's usage text, still says that only refutations report a non-success status, but trials now also record frontend refusal statuses such as `INPUT_ERROR` and `UNSUPPORTED`. Fix: add that refusals from the application and from the SQL frontend report their status, and that the diagnostic does not stop with a traceback.

New kernel-gate module: `requireLibraryRoots` and `explicitArtifacts` now decide which installed and caller `.olean` files the gates import, and refuse duplicate installed modules; owner review required. Fix: have the owner review the root ordering, the duplicate-module refusal and the exact artifact selection.

`importData` now passes explicit artifacts from `explicitArtifacts` to `importModulesCore` instead of using Lean's search-path resolution; owner review required. Fix: have the owner review the changed import resolution of the kernel gate.

`checkProof` takes a separate model library root, and its trusted search path changed from the builtin path plus one library to the validated application and model roots; owner review required. Fix: have the owner review the new argument order and search-path order.

The bundle checker now uses `Belay.Sqlite.Codec` instead of `StructuralCodec`, builds declarations against `Belay.Sqlite` type names, and takes a separate model library root; owner review required. Fix: have the owner review the codec replacement and the new trusted roots.

The verification target now imports its model from `Belay.Sqlite.SqlExecution` and opens `Belay.Sqlite`, so the names in `VerificationConditions` resolve to the external package; owner review required. Fix: have the owner review that the contract still refers to the intended model definitions.

`export_bundle` now uses both installed libraries as the omitted trusted closure for the exported proof; owner review required. Fix: have the owner review that the export omits only declarations the checker supplies from those two roots.
Bundle verification now passes both libraries to contract compilation and to the bundle checker; owner review required. Fix: have the owner review the changed approval and checker invocation path.

The comment, and the module docstring at line 9, still say that trusted modules resolve "only from the sysroot and verifier library", but `schemaEnvironment` now resolves them from the sysroot, the application library and the model library. Fix: say "the sysroot, application library and model library", as `docs/data-path.md` now does, and update the same phrase in `GateCore.lean:64`.

The mechanical rename of `library` to `libraries` left broken text: "its trusted-libraries imports" here, and "toolchain/libraries identity" in `migration_check/stage_store.py`. Fix: write "imports from the trusted libraries" and "toolchain and library identity".

The docstring "A relative libraries path cannot redirect..." is broken English. Also, the `libraries` argument of `KernelCase.check` replaces only the application root, not both. Fix: rename the argument to `application_library` and write "A relative application library path cannot redirect the checker's trusted imports."
